smells.finding: apply_layer1() is ~55 lines of function body (lines 228-295) doing a per-axis loop that computes density_component, mass_component, explained, residual, and a 4-term quadrature sigma. It is a single cohesive responsibility (not a grab-bag), well-commented and vectorized, but could be split into small helpers (e.g. _density_component(), _mass_component(), _combine_sigma()) for readability. Non-blocking observation, not a defect.
No classes beyond the 6-field frozen DensityFit dataclass, a plain value object.

No meaningful duplication; shared logic (_season_key_series) is factored out once; test axis-parametrization (TestHonestNoOp, TestMexicoMonacoResidualConsistency) uses pytest.mark.parametrize instead of copy-pasted test bodies.
Each function operates on its own passed-in df/params; no reaching into another module's internals.
DensityFit groups (axis, beta, se, n, n_car_seasons, applied) as a deliberate named value object, the opposite of an unencapsulated data clump.
Axis identity is a bare string throughout (DENSITY_SENSITIVE_AXES/MASS_SENSITIVE_AXES as frozensets of str, axis: str params) rather than an enum/domain type.

override.repo_standard: src/physics/weekend_state/frame.py's AXES list (g1, already-reviewed/merged) establishes axis identity as a plain list[str] constant -- the store's own column names.
override.reason: layer1_physics.py consumes frame.AXES directly and must key into the same DataFrame columns it defines; introducing a parallel enum/domain type here would fragment the axis-identity convention across g1/g2 for no behavioral gain, since the underlying data (SQL column names) is already string-typed at its source.

smells.finding: Max 4 params per function (fit_density_betas, apply_layer1, mexico_monaco_residual_consistency), all with sensible defaults.
Adding a new axis category touches at most the two frozensets in this one file; no cross-file ripple.
Single responsibility (the explained-physics/density-mass layer); no unrelated concerns bundled in.
pandas .groupby().transform() chains are idiomatic vectorized pandas, not deep object-navigation chains in the Fowler OO sense.

DEFAULT_WEEKEND_KEY = ("year", "round_idx") is defined at module level (line 138) but never referenced anywhere in the module or its test -- unused generality left in for a hypothetical future caller. Non-blocking; worth deleting or wiring up in g3/g4 if genuinely needed there.

The module's extensive docstrings explain WHY (physical justification: why not naive divide-by-rho, F=ma mass-elasticity reasoning, the Mexico/Monaco setup-confound caveat) rather than papering over unclear code; this matches CREW_CONTEXT's 'units, bounds, and invariants must be explicit' physics rule.
